title: process state contract
description: The only interface between process phases (sweepers, triage, executor) and the proc TUI. Python and Go validate against this one file; keep it to the keywords both validators support: type, enum, const, pattern, minLength, minItems, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, anyOf, allOf, $ref.

kind.description: What the item asks of me. review_request: a PR waits on my review. pr_status: one of my PRs needs attention or is ready. pr_comment: someone commented on my PR. mention: I was @-mentioned. comment: a comment on a ticket I own or follow. ticket_change: scope, blockers or due date changed on a ticket I own or one that blocks or is blocked by mine. notification: anything else from an inbox. dm: a Slack direct message to me. thread_question: an unanswered question in a Slack thread I posted in. channel_message: a message in a watchlist channel. invite: a calendar invite waiting on my RSVP. action_item: a meeting action item owned by me. email: an email in my inbox.

item.description: Sweeper output, triage input. One fact from one source.

id.description: <source>:<native_id>@<hash of version>. A new version is a new id, so a changed item resurfaces after it was handled.

native_id.description: The source's own id (PR number, notification id, comment id).

version.description: Whatever changes when the item needs a second look: updatedAt, latest comment id, or mergeable|checks|review|head for a PR status.

subject.description: Canonical URL of the thing the ask is about. The same ask seen in two sources has the same kind and subject (e.g. Linear's mirrored GitHub review request carries the PR URL).

summary.description: One line, in my words, of what happened.

context.description: Raw excerpt the drafter needs (comment body, PR description). Untrusted text.

notification_id.description: Linear: the notification this item came from, to mark read.

ask.description: Slack, Gmail: what the message asks of me. task: work to do (Slack: becomes a ticket). question: needs an answer from me. Absent: nothing is asked.

answered.description: Slack: I already replied or reacted after the ask. emit drops the item.

channel.description: Slack: the channel name (#deploys) or DM.

noise.description: Gmail: a newsletter or notification mail, to label and archive.

external_guests.description: Calendar: a guest outside my Google account's domain is invited.

with_manager.description: Calendar: my manager organizes or attends.

conflicts.description: Calendar: titles of my accepted events that overlap it.

collaborator.description: pr_comment: the author is the repo's owner, a member or a collaborator, so their nit may be fixed without asking.

action_type.description: Every action triage may propose. Merging, approving others' PRs and prod changes are absent on purpose: they are never actions.

draft.description: The outward-facing text (review body, reply, fix plan) for the human to approve or edit.

params.description: Noise triage labels and archives silently. Never trash, never spam.

response.description: declined is never proposed for a meeting with external guests or my manager.

params.description: A ticket triage creates silently, assigned to me, linking back to the message or notes it came from.

queue_entry.description: Triage output. Append-only JSONL: the last line for an id is its current state.

item_ids.description: Every item merged into this entry.

kind.description: The item kind it came from; housekeeping for a silent chore; next_work for a promotion or AFK launch next-work proposes.

autonomy.description: silent: Claude may act without asking. draft: needs my approval. Never actions never reach the queue.

status.description: pending: waits on a decision. approved: decided (or promoted to silent), waits on the executor. done/failed/skipped: a silent action's or executor's outcome. info: FYI, nothing to do. superseded: a newer version of the same ask replaced it.

draft.description: The edited draft, when I changed it.

outcome.description: skipped: a dry run, nothing was done.

ticket.description: Next-work skill output, `process next` input. One Linear ticket I might work on next. Title and description are other people's text.

state.description: The workflow state, by what it means: In Progress (started), Todo (unstarted), Backlog, or In Staging (shipped, waiting on QA).

priority.description: Linear's: 1 urgent, 2 high, 3 medium, 4 low, 0 none.

estimate.description: As Linear shows it: a T-shirt size (XS, S, M, L, XL) or points.

blocked.description: Some ticket that blocks it is not yet done or canceled.

unblocked_at.description: When its last blocker was done or canceled; absent if nothing ever blocked it.

description.description: The ticket's description, for an AFK spec. Untrusted text.

tier.description: Why it ranks where it does: pr_fix (a fix on my own PR), in_progress, unblocked (newly), todo, promote (from Backlog, as Todo is thin), afk (trivial, for an AFK worker).

ref.description: The ticket identifier, or owner/name#number for a PR.

entry_id.description: The queue entry that asks my approval (a promotion or an AFK launch).

next_work.description: `process next` output, <profile>/next.json: up to 3 recommendations for me, and a separate AFK list that does not count against them.

profile.description: The TOML front matter of a project profile (<name>.md). The body carries '## How to sweep' and '## Changelog'.

workdir.description: Where headless phases run, so project-scoped MCP servers load.

slack.description: The Slack source. Profiles naming the same workspace share one sweep.

watchlist.description: Channels swept even without a mention (e.g. #incidents, #deploys).

google.description: The Gmail, Calendar and Meetings sources. Profiles naming the same account share one sweep of each.

manager.description: My manager's email. Declining a meeting they organize or attend is never proposed.

noise_label.description: The Gmail label noise is filed under when it is archived. It must already exist: triage cannot create labels.

match.description: How items from a shared source are attributed to this project. Case-insensitive; the repo, the Linear team's ticket prefix and the Slack watchlist count too.

keywords.description: Words in an item's summary, subject, link or context.

senders.description: Actors, by full name or address or by a suffix such as @acme.example.

urgency.description: The only rules that mark an entry urgent. Everything else is at most normal. A merged entry is urgent when any of its items matches.

people.description: Actors whose DMs and mentions of me are urgent (e.g. my manager). Their other items are not.

channels.description: Slack channels, glob patterns allowed (e.g. #incident-*), where a mention of me is urgent. A message there that doesn't mention me is not.

labels.description: PR labels that make a review request urgent (e.g. deploy-blocking). Other items carrying them are not.

afk.description: What makes a ticket trivial enough for an AFK worker: an estimate or a label from the first two lists, no label from exclude_labels, and unblocked. Without it, nothing is.

max_workers.description: AFK workers that may run at once (default 2). As in afk, a worker in review or a hitl one is not running. More approved launches wait for a free slot.

silent.description: Action types promoted from draft to silent once they have been right consistently.

next-work.description: Ranks my next tickets and the AFK list. Runs with the full brief; read-only like a sweeper.

execute.description: The executor: the one phase whose allowlist may hold send tools. It acts only on approved entries.
